target.title: refactor: simplify nullish checks with `== null` / `!= null`
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces unnecessary verbosity in nullish checks across the codebase. `x === null || x === undefined` is functionally identical to `x == null`, and `x !== null && x !== undefined` is identical to `x != null`. The shorter form is idiomatic JavaScript and reduces visual noise.

## Why This Change Was Made

Using `== null` (or `!= null`) is the standard idiom for testing both `null` and `undefined` in a single comparison. The longer form adds no safety — `== null` is specifically designed in the language spec to catch both values. Keeping the verbose form across 6 files is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase that already uses `== null` (see `src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.ts:81`, `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.ts:72`, etc.).

## User Impact

None. Zero behavioral change — the comparisons evaluate identically.

## Evidence

All affected test files pass:

```
# git-root test
$ pnpm test -- src/infra/git-root.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

# stable-stringify test
$ pnpm test -- src/agents/stable-stringify.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)

# tool-display-common test
$ pnpm test -- src/agents/tool-display-common.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)

# health test
$ pnpm test -- src/commands/health.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```
